public_rationale: MIR-Bench, published February 14, 2025, reports recurring failures in inferring rules and applying them to new inputs across 15 models [e1]. GSM-∞, published February 7, 2025, finds high accuracy on simpler problems and declining accuracy as required operations increase [e2]. These results support limited reliability in the pre-March 5, 2025 period [e1, e2]. MIR-Bench also finds robustness to incorrect examples, showing successful reasoning alongside the failures [e3]. Earlier context includes an o3 configuration scoring 87.5% on ARC-AGI in December 2024 [e4]. These successes qualify the finding without establishing dependable performance across task variations [e1, e3, e4]. GSM-∞ finds predictable aggregate declines, so its results do not support a literal claim that error rates are statistically unpredictable [e2].
limitations: The February studies are preprints and do not provide complete execution timestamps.
The evidence does not cover every contemporary model or configuration or establish a universal reliability threshold.
Behavioral failures do not establish that abstract representations or reasoning abilities are absent.
The December 2024 ARC-AGI result predates the target period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs still lack a reliable ability to reason over abstractions, as their ongoing unpredictable errors show.

statement.excerpt: • AGI should have reliable ability to reason over abstractions. (Ongoing unpredictable errors in LLMs reflect this.)
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

from_speaker: reliable ability to reason over abstractions
our_interpretation: The empirical claim is that contemporary LLMs still make recurring errors when applying abstract rules. The normative statement about what AGI should possess is not separately scored.
Reliable means dependable performance across relevant new examples and task variations, not literal perfection or an absence of any reasoning ability.
Unpredictable is read as unexpected or inconsistent failures in use, not as a mathematical claim that aggregate error rates cannot be predicted.
With no reporting period supplied, the target is the latest pre-publication evaluation period in 2025, through March 5. Older experiments are context only.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evaluations of contemporary LLMs document recurring failures in applying or inferring abstract rules across new examples, despite success on easier or familiar cases.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, controlled contemporary evaluations establish dependable abstract-rule reasoning across relevant variations, with the alleged recurring failures explained by invalid tests or otherwise not reproduced.

evidence.explanation: MIR-Bench tests fifteen models on deriving outputs from examples of underlying functions. Its controlled evaluations find substantial remaining failures, including in o1-family models, supporting the limited reliability claim.

The generated problems permit controlled changes in reasoning complexity and show recurring failures across models. The predictable aggregate decline also cautions against interpreting unpredictable literally.
The same study finds resilience to incorrect examples. This is material evidence of successful reasoning behavior, limiting any broader inference that LLM abstraction is uniformly fragile or absent.

The benchmark organizers report substantial success on novel abstract tasks, alongside remaining easy-task failures. This is material counterevidence to a claim of no abstraction ability, but it does not establish general reliability and precedes the target period.
